device.modelDescription: Offline, purely static analysis of an npm manifest and lockfile. It answers questions about how a project declares its dependencies -- how many, which are unpinned, which use specifiers that bypass the registry -- and nothing about whether any of them is vulnerable. It performs no network access whatsoever, so it cannot and does not consult any advisory database; it is not `npm audit`. Part of the repo-review composite demo.

actionList.name: audit
actionList.description: Parses the text of a package.json (and optionally its lockfile) and reports: how many dependencies are declared in each section; which ones are not pinned to an exact version; which use a specifier that bypasses the registry's version resolution entirely (a git or http URL, a local file path, `*`, `latest`, or an unbounded `>=`); and, if a lockfile is supplied, how many packages it resolves and whether every direct dependency appears in it. Takes the file text as arguments rather than reading disk, so it is a pure function and can be fed another tool's output. This is a HYGIENE check, not a vulnerability scan: it never reaches the network, so it knows nothing about CVEs or advisories. Do not report its output as a security audit or as equivalent to `npm audit` -- an empty findings list means the manifest is tidy, not that the dependencies are safe.
